title: 'Decline may grow with the rate' rests on one seed and ignores the same-seed A/B noise yardstick
quote: at seed 1 sample accuracy falls 1.5, 3.5 and 8.3 points
explanation: The claim compares Run A across three rates at seed 1 (changes -1.5, -3.5, -8.3 from Table 2). The paper itself says same-seed A and B at 5e-4 are 'closer to two replicates than four', and gives the sample-accuracy pairs A/B as -8.3/-6.7 (seed 1) and -4.7/-9.2 (seed 2). So near-identical runs already differ by 1.6 and 4.5 points; the seed-1 rise (6.8 points from 1e-4 to 5e-4) is only modestly above that yardstick, and the 1e-4 and 2e-4 intervals ([-5.3,2.2], [-7.2,0.0]) overlap heavily with each other and with the 5e-4 interval. If Run B were used instead of A at seed 2, that seed would show 3.7/3.8/9.2, i.e. growth too, so 'one seed' versus 'flat at the other' depends on an arbitrary A/B choice. Seed 2 is called 'almost flat' using A only. No test of rate x change is done, and the three rates share the exam partition and round-0 draw. The hedge 'may' is appropriate, but the one-seed contrast is not evidence of dose-dependence and is stated more suggestively than the intervals allow. Seed-variance (3.2-point replicate gap, +5.3 to -7.3 B-A flip) is acknowledged elsewhere but not applied here.

title: 'At 5e-4 every run declines' is stated for pass@1 but its intervals mostly include zero, and the range covers only A/B
quote: every run declines: pass@1 falls 4.0–11.3 points
explanation: The 4.0-11.3 range is the A/B runs only (A1 -10.0, A2 -4.0, B1 -4.7, B2 -11.3); the other 5e-4 runs in Table 2 fall 6.0, 8.7, 18.0, 21.3 and 22.0, so 'every run' and the range refer to different sets. The pass@1 intervals for A2 [-11.3,3.3] and B1 [-12.0,2.7] include zero, as does no-filter seed 1 [-12.7,1.3]; the claim of a decline in every run is only supported by sample accuracy (which the next clause then qualifies by treating A/B pairs as near-replicates, leaving effectively two independent seeds). The unqualified first clause reads stronger than the evidence, and the paper's own multiplicity/non-independence caveats (Section 3.4) apply.

title: No-filter comparison reported selectively on pass@4 while pass@1 and sample accuracy point both ways
quote: is lower on pass@4 at both seeds
explanation: The text highlights that no-filter is lower than Run A on pass@4 at both seeds (-2.0, -5.3, from Table 3: 40.7 vs 42.7 and 39.3 vs 44.7) while saying the intervals include zero. On round-2 pass@1 in the same Table 3 no-filter is higher at seed 1 (27.3 vs 23.3, +4.0) and lower at seed 2 (22.7 vs 27.3, -4.6); sample accuracy changes are -8.2 vs -8.3 (seed 1) and -10.2 vs -4.7 (seed 2). So the direction is not consistent across metrics, and the pass@4 'lower at both seeds' is a metric-specific observation with intervals including zero that is then contrasted with Section 5.2's 'no consistent difference'. Reporting only the pass@4 direction invites a reading (filter helps) that the paper then disclaims; the full pattern (sign flips on pass@1) should be stated, especially since a sign flip between seeds is exactly what the paper calls noise elsewhere.

title: Cap-share decomposition: unspecified run sets, large seed heterogeneity, and tension with the matched finished-accuracy column
quote: attributes 12–30% of the decline to the cap share in the three original seed-1
explanation: (a) The groups are not identifiable from the main text: 'three original seed-1 runs' (A, B, no-filter?), 'two further runs' with shares of -2 and 5%, and 52-72% 'at seed 2' (three runs?), so the six runs in the previous sentence cannot be matched to the percentages; Table 1 gives cap-hit only for Run A, so '2-14 points' cannot be checked from the tables. (b) The cap share explains 12-30% at one seed and 52-72% at the other, a spread that makes the headline 'finished accuracy carries the change' seed-dependent rather than a property of the learning rate; no uncertainty is attached to any percentage, and Table 1's cap-hit rises for Run A are small (43.0 to 46.2 at seed 1, 43.2 to 51.2 at seed 2) for 600 clustered generations. (c) A crude check with Table 1 (sample acc = finished share x finished accuracy, capped generations wrong) gives for A at seed 2 a nearly unchanged finished accuracy (about 0.54 to 0.54), yet the matched column reports -5.5, larger than the total sample-accuracy fall (-4.7); at 1e-4 A1 the matched finished change (-4.3) is larger than the sample change (-1.5) with no cap rise. Because the matched measure 'conditions on which problems finish after training', the 'finished accuracy lost' figures and the decomposition percentages do not obviously describe the same quantity, and the reader cannot reconcile them without the supplementary tables.

title: 'Finished accuracy carries the whole change' at 1e-4/2e-4 not supported by intervals
quote: At 10−4 and 2 × 10−4 the cap-hit share does not
explanation: The continuation says finished accuracy carries the whole change at these rates. But in Table 2 the matched finished intervals at 1e-4 (A1 [-9.6,1.1], A2 [-9.2,2.3], A3 [-6.0,4.7]) and 2e-4 (A1 [-8.9,0.5], A2 [-10.1,1.0]) all include zero, and the sample-accuracy changes are mostly not distinguishable from zero. At 2e-4 the cap share actually falls by 2-3.5 points (40.8% and 39.7% against 43.0-43.2%), which should make unfinished-generation loss negative, not zero. A statement of attribution is made where no decline is established.

title: Patch-control numbers inconsistent between prose, Table 2 and the stated prevalence
quote: (recomputed from the saved generations; Table 2 lists run-log values that
explanation: Section 4.3 reports B minus A at seed 1 as +0.0 [-2.7,+2.7] from recomputed generations, while Table 2 (-3.3 for A,1 and -4.0 for B,1) gives -0.7, and the Table 2 intervals for those rows come from the same table whose caption says the round values were recomputed 'except six'. The same table therefore mixes run-log values and recomputed values for the headline control comparison, and a reader cannot reproduce the quoted B-A figures or intervals from Table 2 alone. Separately, the prevalence argument is arithmetically loose: 0.50-0.73% of generations containing \dfrac is about 14-20 of 2,800 generations (350 problems x k=8), yet the kept pools differ by only 3-4 examples; the step from generations to pool entries (only generations that flip under the patch and are otherwise correct) is not given. The paired intervals for B-A at 1e-5 (about +/-2.7) are also much narrower than the 12.6-point B-A swing observed at 5e-4, so 'could not detect an effect' depends on the identical-seed, near-identical-output structure rather than on any power calculation (the paper's ~10-point detectable effect does not apply to paired B-A).
source_section: 4.3 The Patch Control Could Not Detect an Effect

title: Statement that 5e-4 runs vs. 'rise in cap-hit share only at 5e-4' relies on a few-point differences without uncertainty
explanation: Table 3 and the surrounding text state that train-on-gold is 'followed by a much larger decline (pass@4 down about 21 points at both seeds)'. The arithmetic matches (-20.7, -20.6), but the conclusion that this cannot be verifier error rests on a bound 'from below only' that covers boxed answers, while 14% of round-2 generations without \boxed are acknowledged as uncovered and the model has moved to $-delimited reference style (5% to 98%). A style shift away from \boxed is precisely the failure mode the V/V' audit is about, so 'unlikely to be mainly verifier error' is an inference without an upper bound; the 'cannot bound it from above' admission is correct but the sentence still sets the expectation. The gold arm is further used in 4.6 as the positive gate with the same unresolved question, so the gate's failure (49.2 -> 17.0) cannot distinguish a real training defect from a format-grading effect.
